source: Be silent! I believe my brother's spirit. Hamlet, grab him.
Oh, come now, Bernardo. You don't actually want to kill me. All this exhausting, confusing drivel. What does it mean to you?
You truly believe that what the Mad Prince says is real?
All this is just a misunderstanding. The insane delusions of your insane friend here, who hijacked a community event to make his final stand.
Be silent! I believe His Majesty's spirit. Hamlet, grab him.
No, thank you. I don't like to be touched.
He's—he's dead?
H-he's not even touching them!
I warned you, Ophelia. I don't feel like playing anymore.
Let's call this round a draw and return to the beginning. That way, I won't have to punish you.
Or maybe I'll teach you how much further this pain can go.
Even then, I won't give up. I'm going to keep coming at you.
How do you want me to kill Hamlet next time, love? Shall we watch him gurgle to death on his own bile and blood? Shall we hang him and watch his face turn blue?
I wonder how many pieces of you I can break before you die. Shall I begin with your wrists and ankles and go from there?
Snapping every little bone like a winter twig, working my way up to your neck...
Oh, I simply can't wait! We're going to have a lovely time.
You think I'd let you do that?
I can do anything I want to you. There's nothing you can do to stop me.
And this story? This is mine. I will not allow you to steal it from me.
Now, Ophelia, I simply must congratulate you on a heroic attempt. It was nearly well-executed.
But, well, nearly doesn't count for very much, does it?
Die... die, die, die!
You demon! You can come after me, but so help the witless devil who comes for my family!
My family--
You demon. You can come for all of us, but so help the witless fool who comes after Hamlet.
Is he really...
Can it be over?
The world has come undone. Now a new story begins.

source: I thought I heard something.
King Hamlet!
It is with my last fragments of will that I appear to you. I do not know how long I can linger.
I'm sorry. I didn't think the plan would turn out like this.
There has to be another way. Something else I can try. Killing him didn't work.
But maybe...
Maybe there's another way.
No, Ophelia. There is no other way.
What he says is true.
I know that now more than ever. The confines surrounding this world are insurmountable.
Ophelia, there will be no way out from this.
I don't understand. What's the point, Hamlet? Of any of this?
I just want to give up, the way you did, and be done with it.
I'm so tired.
The only way out is to sentence some of my friends to die.
No matter what I do, someone is going to die. I can't save them! I can't do it!
There's no good ending. There's no good world! I've tried everything I could...
That kind of world was never a possible outcome for you, Ophelia.
No such world of eternal bliss exists. For you, or for anyone on earth.
And it never shall.
But there is something even more powerful.
It is the oldest, most primal power of humankind.
The power to choose with kindness and wisdom is the only thing separating human beings from utter darkness.
You have seen the possibilities of this universe. Now it's up to you to envision its fate.
Let me be clear. There is no perfect world to be found.
But the choice between worlds is a power so critical as to be divinely given, is it not? Freedom of will! The first and last gift granted to Eve herself!
Yes... free will is a sword to cut through the darkness. It is a small boat we cling to in this lifelong storm!
In that, Ophelia, is everything. You must choose, and you must then live in the world which comes from it.
You must do the thing you fear most, and move forward rather than back.
I don't want to leave. As long as I stay here, it's as though there's something new I can try...
Some new way out to discover.
What if I burn the book? What if I destroy it?
You would punish Quince. But you would condemn every human heart in this castle to their fates. You'd abandon them.
I-- This is-- But there has to be another way! A good way--a best path!
No. Perfection is impossible. No such world could ever exist. Not so long as imperfect human beings fill it.
Use the Book of Fates, Ophelia. Do what I could not.
Refuse to give up!
I... I will. Much as I don't want to.
I promise.
Not long now...
If only I had known the kind of strength you possess when I was alive, child.
Though your body might be frail, you are brilliant as the sun.
Someday many years hence, let us play a game of chess together sometime.
Or walk amongst those verdant, shimmering gardens I once slept in peacefully...
I... hope it is permissible that I call you a friend in death, though I hardly knew you in life.
Of course. Of course it is.
I'm certain we'll see one another again.
It is the end.
And I am not afraid.
Goodbye, King Hamlet.
I'll find a way to make all this worthwhile. Whatever that end is. I promise.
You were sorely missed at Hamlet's departure this morning.
Apologies, my lord. I didn't make the ship in time.
Hmph. Never mind it. There are always alternatives.
We've got a long journey ahead of us.
My lord, my ladies, welcome aboard, your excellencies.
By your faces, I don't recall having sailed with any of you before, save His Majesty here.
My name is Captain Norby. We'll be three days at sea, and—
Yes, I've a burning question! When is supper?
Guilda, we've only just left port. It's not quite noon.
Lunch, then?
I'm sure provisions can, er, be arranged for you.
Guilda! Honestly, you're so common sometimes...
I wouldn't even—hrgh... Oh, no.
Lady Rosencrantz, are you... all right?
I've forgotten how horribly seasick I get. P-please, excuse me.
...Farewell to Denmark. Farewell to that awful tower.
May we be delivered to England as swiftly as possible.
(The King has tasked me with ensuring Hamlet's demise before we return to Denmark.)
(That could change the fate of Elsinore... but I'm not certain I can bring myself to do that.)
(I should investigate while I'm here.)
This is all meaningless to me. I'm only here to have fun!
Say, you said I was going to die here, didn't you?
Well, that's foreboding.
Say, Ophelia, have you ever looked at the stars at sea?
They're so much bigger and brighter!
I don't mind if I live or die, but we should look at the stars together!
All right, Guilda. I'll be there.
(She won't survive past tomorrow if I can't find a way to keep her and Rosie alive.)
(Yet another task lies before me.)
...Hi, Ophelia.
What're you doing up here alone?
Waiting for you! I told you we'd meet, didn't I?
Hi, Ophelia. I slept in late.
Fancy a walk in the gardens?
I thought you'd come find me. Let's stroll a while.
Why here? Why this place?
I just come here to think sometimes. That's all.
I had the oddest feeling.
I think Hamlet's angry with us. With me.
And I don't know what things will be like when we next go ashore.
And I don't know what things will be like in a little while.
...I think your intuition is correct.
Well, it's all right. I always knew the fun would end eventually.
It had to. Rosie and I always move on at some point.
We sort of—go where we go, and meet who we meet, and when the party's concluded, on we move.
Say, Ophelia. Do you think we would have liked England if we'd made it there?
Say, Ophelia. I don't think I want to go back to Wittenberg, where we all went to school.
Do you think you'd like it there?
I don't think I can say. I've never been. And—now I likely never shall.
You know, I don't really even believe in it. England, I mean.
Every time we try to go there, something happens.
Last time, our carriage broke down. Lovely detour to Paris we had. And this time, pirates.
I'm not certain England really exists at this point.
It's just a conspiracy of cartographers, you mean?
Yes! That's exactly it!
Now there's no telling where we'll end up. And there isn't even anything to drink.
What kind of monstrously sober pirates take over a ship and don't even bring liquor with them?
These pirates are far more efficient and businesslike than I was led to believe they'd be.
Oh, there's a wineskin stashed under the helm. I noticed earlier.
It's over there.
You know, I think there's a big, large life ahead of you.
You're like a fish in a little pond. One of the pretty fish, that is.
But some day, you're going to realize you can get past the log at the other end of it.
And then you'll be free! Free to swim all the way to the sea!
I think river fish die when they meet the sea.
Yes! In a brilliant blaze of glory! Go out blazing, Ophelia!
Maybe... it's time for me to strike out and do that, too.
With the situation in the castle, there's no telling what'll happen. And there isn't even anything to drink.
That's why these Danes are at each others' throats constantly. They're all so dreadfully sober.
Isn't this part of the world famous for its halls full of glory and drink?
You haven't looked in the kitchen beside the hearth, have you?
That's where Irma keeps all the castle wine.
Y-you're serious?
Ophelia! You beautiful, marvelous, lavender-coated little sugarplum!
Ooh, I'm so happy I could kiss you!
Oh, is that so?
(So we've come to this point again.)
W-well, actually...
Since we're in the company of unholy people, and that seems an appropriate time for confessions...
Since we're in the garden, and that seems an appropriate place for confessions...
I've had a little fancy for you whenever I've visited Elsinore over the years. But I've only ever known you from afar.
I think the only time we ever spoke was across the dining table in the great hall.
You always seemed so graceful, but sad, in a quiet way. You stood apart from everyone.
I always thought that if I knew you better, maybe I'd be able to give you a kiss that would make you smile.
A-and now, well, here we are.
B-but if you don't want to, we'll still be friends, and I won't be mad!
Kiss Guildenstern?

source: Your cheeks are all red.
Gah. I feel all warm.
It is August.
I suppose.
Ooh! So you did like it!
Well, yes. I like you, Guilda. I wish we had more time together.
